subject: the 60-second preliminary screen
preheader: speed helps only when the assumptions stay visible.
headline: Use a fast first pass to decide which properties deserve deeper work.
body: Many listings will not meet a particular investor's rules after property-specific expenses and financing are entered, but there is no universal pass rate. Market, property, evidence quality, financing, and the investor's own targets all change the result.

A slow first pass limits how many candidates you can compare. A fast one is useful only when it keeps the assumptions visible and leaves appraisal, inspection, lender, tax, legal, and investment decisions to the appropriate evidence and professionals.

Use the preliminary screen to prioritize which properties deserve current comps, a local tax bill, an insurance quote, condition work, and written loan terms. Do not treat it as an automatic rejection or approval workflow.

That's the whole pitch for TrueCap. Paste an address and review cap rate, cash-on-cash, DSCR, NOI, selected-rule fit, and a secondary Screening Index in about 60 seconds. The index is triage context, not an automatic buy/pass verdict. Verify the assumptions before relying on the result.
Pick any random listing right now. Paste it in. See how fast it really is.
